sources.citation: real-world (product class), makers' listings seen in search summaries, 2026-11-18, not read in full: 15 W, 120 V surface-mounted LED fixtures list power factors from about 0.7 to 0.98 on makers' sheets, several at or above 0.9; 0.9 is taken (carried as a lagging displacement, ADR 0021 L3). Fixtures are listed to UL 1598 (cited by number).

game-design inside the P4 pre-audit's labelled figure (constant power from 108 V, dropout about 90 V; not a datasheet reading): the driver stops below 90 V and, once stopped, starts again at 95 V, a 5 V hysteresis band chosen so it never chatters at the edge. Both lie below the 108 V the pre-audit holds constant power from, and the rated 120 V is above both.

game-design: a square wall light drawn as its 120 × 120 mm bounding box, 95 mm deep from a device box's back wall (the yoke mount's origin) to 35 mm proud of a single-gang box's opening; its push-in terminal block (hot, neutral, ground) sits inside the gang, 40 mm off the back wall. The body covers the box's opening, as a fixture's canopy does, so a splice inside the box would sit inside the body. Not modelled on a product.

game-design: the light's strap screws to a device box's two device-mounting holes, as a light wall-mounted fixture may (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 314.27(A)(1) Exception, cited by number, allows a wall luminaire of not more than 3 kg (6 lb) on other boxes when secured by at least two screws, which the inspector does not check; the fixture's mass isn't modelled), so it fits the deviceYoke mount, centred on the gang: its origin 37 mm left of and 24 mm below the gang's corner. The ceiling boxes offer no mount yet. Its one strap contact joins its ground terminal to a metal box's chassis.

game-design (plan D3: a yoke-screw bond is game-design): 5 mΩ from the grounding terminal through the strap and its two mounting screws to a metal box's tapped ears, ten or more times the screw class's 0.2 to 0.5 mΩ for a torqued copper conductor (NBS BSS 103) because the joint is plated steel on steel under small screws at no marked torque; not measured. On a box with no chassis terminal (or a nonmetallic one) the contact adds nothing.

game-design: real fixtures of the class have pigtail leads spliced in the box; a device's own leads can't be spliced in the game, so the light has a push-in (spring-cage) terminal block, one 14 or 12 AWG solid copper conductor per pole, not for aluminium, a 10 ± 1 mm strip and a 9 mm cage depth, as some fixtures' wiring compartments do. Its contact (0.3 mΩ, ADR 0018's spring-cage example inside NBS BSS 128's 1.5 mΩ), heat path (0.02 W/K) and clamp heat capacity (0.35 J/K) are the 2.5 mm² spring-cage terminal block's (tb.quennick-sc25), applied as game-design.
game-design: conductors come from the box behind the light and enter each pole of the block along -z; not modelled on a product.
